newsitem.title: USA: Weyerhaeuser agrees to sell mortgage unit.
newsitem.headline: Weyerhaeuser agrees to sell mortgage unit.

text.p: Weyerhaeuser Co said it had reached an agreement to sell its Weyerhaeuser Mortgage Co subsidiary to WMC Acquisition Co., an entity formed by Apollo Management L.P. and Spring Mountain Escrow Inc.
Terms of the sale were not disclosed.
Weyerhaeuser Mortgage Co., based in Woodland Hills, Calif., focuses on residential mortgage loan origination and servicing. It has 1,500 employees in 58 offices in 15 states.
Weyerhaeuser said in September it had retained Goldman Sachs & Co to explore the possible sale of the mortgage unit.

"We felt that the mortgage company could benefit from ownership that's more strongly focused on financial services," Weyerhaeuser spokesman Frank Mendizabal said. "We continue to focus on our principal business segments, which are pulp, paper and packaging; timberlands and wood products; and real estate."
Apollo and its affiliates constitute the main investment vehicle for Wall Street financier Leon Black, who has interests in businesses ranging from commercial real estate to ski resorts.
Spring Mountain Escrow is the largest independent escrow company in California.

The mortgage unit comprises most of Weyerhaeuser's smallest business division, financial services, which had operating earnings of $8 million last year on revenues of $205 million, less than two percent of the company's total.
Over the first eight months of 1996, the unit originated $2.1 billion in residential mortgages and the unit has a capacity to originate $5 billion in mortgages annually.
The unit services a portfolio of about $4 billion in residential mortgages concentrated in California, Hawaii, Arizona and other Western states.
